tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y): The starting coordinates for `left_click_drag`.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

# usage: run-case.sh <case> <launch-status> <on|off> <page:normal|throws> <seconds>
# Runs the scratch copy of the worktree's app once, with its own data folder
# (seeded from the seed run, automatic reports on or off), against the local
# stand-in for JusPrin's server and Sentry, for <seconds>, then stops that
# app only. Prints what the stand-in received.
C=$1; ST=$2; REP=$3; PAGE=$4; SECS=$5
L=/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/75a11bff-4206-4fd9-a7c4-4494377a5bf7/scratchpad/live
APP=$L/JusPrinTest.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
PORT=8761; PAGEPORT=8762
D=$L/$C; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D
if [ "$C" != seed ]; then
  cp -R $L/seed/data $D/data; rm -rf $D/data/log
  python3 -I - "$D/data/JusPrin2.conf" "$REP" <<'PY'
import json, sys
path, rep = sys.argv[1:]
text = open(path).read()
data = json.loads(text[:text.rfind("}") + 1])
data.setdefault("app", {})["jusprin_report_errors_automatically"] = "true" if rep == "on" else "false"
open(path, "w").write(json.dumps(data, indent=4))
PY
else

---
name: drive-app-with-posted-key-events
description: "Drive the built JusPrin app headlessly (even with the screen locked) by posting CGEvents to its pid with a tiny Swift tool; keys work, mouse clicks do not, and the send dialog is reachable by keyboard."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6b96dccc-1cb4-4f72-9de4-3ecee4b28e74
  modified: 2026-09-08T05:58:16.222Z
---

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]].

content.content:
## Phase 2: Sentry's own SDKs (in progress, uncommitted, same worktree)
- deps/Sentry/Sentry.cmake: sentry-native 0.17.5 release zip (sha256 64d1e29f…), crashpad backend, SENTRY_TRANSPORT none; deps/CMakeLists.txt +2 lines (include, dep_Sentry). Rebase sim v2.5.0 -> upstream/main e76b4d676c: deps/CMakeLists.txt auto-merges; same 4 conflicts as without the change.
- Built into scratch prefix scratchpad/depsprefix (not the shared deps). Worktree build uses -Dsentry_DIR=<that>/lib/cmake/sentry. Trap: never put two paths in CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH: src/libslic3r/CMakeLists.txt:686 sets OpenCASCADE_DIR from it and picks Homebrew/other OCCT, full rebuild + Standard_Failure::what compile error.
- Support/SentryEvent.{hpp,cpp} (replaces SentryEnvelope): DSN parse, fingerprint, event per report, scrubbed_sentry_event (no user/install id, home -> "~" in every string, infer_ip never, page debug_meta restored).
- Support/SentryClient.{hpp,cpp}: start_sentry from JusPrin::startup_begin; consent = automatic setting (Preferences + dialog call sentry_follow_setting); dialog report = give/capture/revoke; transport over Slic3r::Http; atexit sentry_close; breadcrumbs from page message types + finished tool calls (AgentHost/HomeHost set_step_listener).
- Pages: @sentry/browser 11.10.0 (2026-10-28) in AgentUI + HomeUI; WebShared/errorReports.ts; event handed to app in report_error {error, where, event}; Console/BrowserSession integrations off; click crumbs lose [attr] parts. Page tests pass (832, 168), guards proven failing.
- Release workflow: sentry-cli 3.8.2 debug-files upload per OS; secrets SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_URL, SENTRY_ORG, SENTRY_PROJECT (skip with warning if no token). Mac binary has symtab+unwind only (no line numbers).

content.text:
Error reports now go through Sentry's own libraries: sentry-native 0.17.5 in the app, and @sentry/browser 11.10.0 in the Agent and Home pages. On my Mac, against the local stand-in, each case below produced the result listed, except the Report button press. That case is still waiting for the screen to unlock. Nothing is committed, and Windows and Linux are not built or tested.

**What was built**
- **App failures.** Each one becomes one Sentry event with its stack, the list of loaded modules and the machine details. It also carries breadcrumbs: the pages' recent message types and the tool calls that finished. The release, the `doing` and `os` tags, and grouping that ignores request ids are kept. The project address still comes only from the `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN` secret.
- **Page failures.** The browser library catches the error and builds the event, but the page doesn't send it. It hands the event to the app, which asks the person (or not, when automatic reports are on) and sends it. I chose this because the consent setting and the dialog live in the app, and so no project address goes into the page bundles.
- **Turned off because they would break the dialog's promises:**
  - console lines, which can hold what the person typed;
  - sessions;
  - the attribute text in click breadcrumbs, which can name a project;
  - query strings in request breadcrumbs;
  - the install id the SDK adds as `user`;
  - the home folder, replaced by `~` everywhere;
  - storing the IP address.
- **Crashes.** These are captured as minidumps, Sentry's memory snapshot of the crashed process.

**What I tested (Mac, stand-in only)**
- With reports on, an app failure gives one event: 32 stack frames, 1,060 modules, no user, no home folder.
- With reports on, a Home page error gives one JavaScript event with 5 breadcrumbs and none of the app's modules.
- With reports off, the same page error sends nothing.
- With reports on, a crash uploads one minidump with no user.
- With reports off, a crash sends nothing. The next start with reports on didn't send it either, within the 40 seconds that run lasted.
- All test suites pass: 189 app cases, 612 agent bridge cases, 832 Agent page tests and 168 Home page tests. clang-tidy passes on all 22 changed C++ files. Each new guard test fails when its fix is removed.
- **Not yet tested:** pressing "Report to JusPrin team" with reports off. A background run is waiting for the screen to unlock, for up to 45 minutes.

**Sentences that are now untrue** (I did not change them):
- In the report dialog:
  - "Each report holds only the lines under ‘See what the report contains’…"
  - "That is the whole report…"

name: JusPrin release

# Builds JusPrin from one commit and uploads the files to a DRAFT GitHub
# release. It never publishes anything.
#
# - The version is the one in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp, and
#   the draft is tagged jusprin/v<version>, as JusPrin 1.4.0 was (the repo
#   still holds OrcaSlicer's own v2.x tags). GitHub creates that tag only when
#   the draft is published, by hand, on the Releases page. JusPrin's update
#   check reads the public release list, which never includes drafts, so
#   users see nothing until then.
# - It stops if that version is already released, is not above every
#   released JusPrin version, or its tag already exists
#   (Packaging/release.mjs), and if
#   Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md, the notes the draft starts with and
#   that the app shows under "What's new", is missing.
# - It also stops if the guide was not checked for this version
#   (docs/guide/checked-version.txt, written by scripts/check_guide.py
#   --ask-ai; see docs/guide/README.md), unless "Release without the guide
#   check" is ticked. Then the draft's title says the guide was not checked.
# - Running it again for the same version replaces the draft's files.
# - Files: Windows x64 installer and portable zip, macOS universal disk image,
#   Linux x64 AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - Only the release publisher can run it: the repo variable
#   JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER, or kennethjiang when it is unset.
# - Signing: macOS when "sign_macos" is ticked, with the Apple secrets JusPrin
#   1.x used. The box starts ticked: Homebrew's cask rules reject a Mac app
#   that is not signed and notarised. A release started by pushing a branch
#   is never signed. Windows builds are unsigned. An unsigned draft says so
#   in its title.
#
# Start it from Actions > JusPrin release > Run workflow (the file must also
# be on the default branch for that button), or by pushing a branch named
# jusprin-release/<anything>.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign_macos:
        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
        type: boolean
        default: true
      skip_guide_check:
        description: 'Release without the guide check'
        type: boolean
        default: false
  push:
    branches:
      - 'jusprin-release/**'

permissions:
  contents: write   # create the draft and upload its files
  actions: read

concurrency:
  group: jusprin-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: Check the version
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.check.outputs.tag }}
      prerelease: ${{ steps.check.outputs.prerelease }}
      draft_id: ${{ steps.check.outputs.draft_id }}
      guide_checked: ${{ steps.guide.outputs.checked }}
    steps:
      - name: Only the release publisher
        env:
          PUBLISHER: ${{ vars.JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER || 'kennethjiang' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_ACTOR" != "$PUBLISHER" ]; then
            echo "::error::Only @$PUBLISHER may make a JusPrin release (this run is @$GITHUB_ACTOR's)."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin
            docs/guide

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Test the release checks
        run: node --test src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.test.mjs

      - name: Check the version against the releases
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=100" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json"
          gh api --paginate "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/matching-refs/tags/" --jq '.[].ref' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt"
          node src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.mjs check src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json" "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Require the release notes
        run: |
          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}.md"
          if [ ! -s "$notes" ]; then
            echo "::error::Write $notes first. The draft starts with it and the app shows it under What's new."
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -q '^PLACEHOLDER' "$notes"; then
            echo "::warning::$notes is still the placeholder. Replace it before publishing the draft."
          fi

      - name: Require the guide check
        id: guide
        env:
          SKIP: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.skip_guide_check || false }}
        run: |
          problem=$(node src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.mjs guide src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp \
            docs/guide/checked-version.txt)
          if [ -z "$problem" ]; then
            echo "checked=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [ "$SKIP" = "true" ]; then
            echo "::warning::\"Release without the guide check\" is ticked, so the release goes on. $problem"
            echo "checked=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "::error::$problem Or tick \"Release without the guide check\" on the Run workflow form."
            exit 1
          fi

  build:
    name: Build
    needs: prepare
    uses: ./.github/workflows/jusprin_build_all.yml
    with:
      version: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      sign_macos: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos || false }}
    secrets: inherit

  draft:
    name: Upload to the draft release
    needs: [prepare, build]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Optional approval gate: give the "release" environment a required
    # reviewer in the repo settings.
    environment: release
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      TAG: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
      DRAFT_ID: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.draft_id }}
      PRERELEASE: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.prerelease }}
      SIGNED_MACOS: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos || false }}
      GUIDE_CHECKED: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.guide_checked }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging

      - name: Collect the files
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-*
          path: collected
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Checksums
        run: |
          mkdir dist
          # The per-architecture Mac bundles only feed the universal app.
          find collected -maxdepth 1 -type f ! -name 'JusPrin_Mac_bundle_*' -exec cp {} dist/ \;
          (cd dist && sha256sum -- * > SHA256SUMS.txt)
          cat dist/SHA256SUMS.txt

      - name: Create or update the draft
        run: |
          title="JusPrin $VERSION"
          if [ "$SIGNED_MACOS" != "true" ]; then
            title="$title (UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish)"
          fi
          if [ "$GUIDE_CHECKED" != "true" ]; then
            title="$title (guide not checked)"
          fi
          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/$VERSION.md"
          prerelease=$([ "$PRERELEASE" = "true" ] && echo --prerelease || echo --prerelease=false)
          if [ -z "$DRAFT_ID" ]; then
            gh release create "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft $prerelease \
              --target "$GITHUB_SHA" --title "$title" --notes-file "$notes"
          else
            # Never touch a published release: release.mjs only reports drafts.
            is_draft=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" --jq .draft)
            if [ "$is_draft" != "true" ]; then
              echo "::error::Release $DRAFT_ID is no longer a draft."
              exit 1
            fi
            gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" \
              -f target_commitish="$GITHUB_SHA" -f name="$title" -F prerelease="$PRERELEASE" \
              -f body="$(cat "$notes")" > /dev/null
            gh release upload "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          fi
          gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=20" \
            --jq ".[] | select(.tag_name == \"$TAG\") | {name, draft, prerelease, target_commitish, html_url, assets: [.assets[].name]}"

name: JusPrin release build

# One platform of a JusPrin release, called by jusprin_release.yml.
#
# The build is OrcaSlicer's: its dependency workflow (build_deps.yml), cached
# under the key OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml uses, and its build
# scripts. Only the packaging is JusPrin's (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging).
# OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml can't be reused as it is: its Linux step looks
# for OrcaSlicer_Linux_V<version>.AppImage, which a JusPrin build never
# writes, and its packaging steps name everything OrcaSlicer.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      os:
        required: true
        type: string
      # x64 (Windows), arm64 or x86_64 (macOS); empty for Linux amd64, as in
      # OrcaSlicer's build_all.yml.
      arch:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      version:
        required: true
        type: string

jobs:
  cache:
    name: Find the deps cache
    # GitHub often has no hosted macOS runner free, and cancels a job that gets
    # none within 15 minutes, so the macOS lookup runs on Linux, as in
    # OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml.
    runs-on: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && 'ubuntu-24.04' || inputs.os }}
    outputs:
      key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
      path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
      hit: ${{ steps.lookup.outputs.cache-hit }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'
      - name: Compute the key
        id: key
        shell: bash
        env:
          # As in OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml. The macOS and Linux trees are
          # OrcaSlicer's and share its cache; OrcaSlicer builds Windows with clang-cl,
          # so JusPrin's cl tree is cached on its own.
          cache_os: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && format('{0}-{1}', inputs.os, inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && format('windows-{0}-msvc', inputs.arch) || format('linux-clang{0}', inputs.arch && format('-{0}', inputs.arch) || '')) }}
          OS: ${{ inputs.os }}
          dep_folder: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && format('/{0}', inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64') && '-arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep' || '/OrcaSlicer_dep' }}
        run: |
          echo "key=${cache_os}-cache-orcaslicer_deps-build-${{ hashFiles('deps/**') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Relative to the workspace, as build_deps.yml takes it.
          echo "path=deps/build${dep_folder}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # The workspace of a hosted macOS job, where build_deps.yml saved the tree.
          if [[ "$OS" == macos-* ]]; then
            echo "macos_workspace=/Users/runner/work/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      # actions/cache matches the path too, so a Linux lookup for macOS names the
      # macOS workspace.
      - name: Look the cache up
        id: lookup
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.macos_workspace || github.workspace }}/${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
          lookup-only: true

  deps:
    name: Build deps
    needs: cache
    if: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.hit != 'true' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_deps.yml
    with:
      cache-key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
      cache-path: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
      valid-cache: false
      os: ${{ inputs.os }}
      arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
      # cl under the Visual Studio generator, which JusPrin's Windows build uses.
      compiler: msvc
      # Stops build_deps.yml before it calls OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      build-deps-only: true
    secrets: inherit

  build:
    name: Build JusPrin
    needs: [cache, deps]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.cache.result == 'success' && (needs.deps.result == 'success' || needs.deps.result == 'skipped') }}
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.os }}
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      # The Sentry project the app's error reports go to, read by
      # JusPrin/sources.cmake; kept out of the public repository.
      JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN: ${{ secrets.JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - name: Load the deps
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
          fail-on-cache-miss: true

      # The same CMake as OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      # The Agent and Home pages are built with npm (JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt).
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # Windows
      - name: Set up MSVC
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        uses: microsoft/setup-msbuild@v3

      - name: Install NSIS
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: choco install nsis

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml calls build_win.bat, but with cl rather than
        # clang-cl. -i installs into build\OrcaSlicer, which the packaging reads.
        run: |
          $deps = (Split-Path "${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}").Replace('\', '/')
          .\build_win.bat -s -i --arch ${{ inputs.arch }} --build-dir build --deps-dir $deps --msvc --msbuild

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/windows_package.ps1 -BuildDir build -Version $env:VERSION `
            -Arch "${{ inputs.arch }}" -OutDir dist

      # macOS: each architecture is built here; jusprin_release.yml joins them
      # into the universal app and the disk image.
      - name: Prepare the Mac
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install libtool
          mkdir -p "${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/${{ inputs.arch }}"
          # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml does, for disk space: keep only the
          # selected Xcode.
          xcode=$(basename "$(cd "$(xcode-select -p)/../.." && pwd -P)")
          sudo find /Applications -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "Xcode_*.app" ! -name "$xcode" -exec rm -rf {} +
          sudo rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Caches/*

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: ./build_release_macos.sh -s -n -x -j 3 -a ${{ inputs.arch }} -t 10.15

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          tar -czf "dist/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_${{ inputs.arch }}.tar.gz" -C "build/${{ inputs.arch }}" OrcaSlicer

      # Linux
      - name: Install the build packages
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        uses: ./.github/actions/apt-install-deps

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          # -s builds the slicer and lays out build/package; JusPrin's AppImage
          # replaces OrcaSlicer's (-i).
          ./build_linux.sh -srlL
          ./scripts/check_appimage_libs.sh ./build/package ./build/package/bin/orca-slicer

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/appimage.sh build/package "$VERSION" \
            "dist/JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_V${VERSION}${{ inputs.arch && format('_{0}', inputs.arch) || '' }}.AppImage"

      # What lets Sentry name the functions in a crash or a report's stack: each
      # executable and library the app ships, with its PDB on Windows, filed by
      # its build id, so the release's own name plays no part. Sentry's address
      # and the token that may upload stay in the repository's secrets. A
      # build without the token uploads nothing and says so.
      - name: Upload debug files to Sentry
        shell: bash
        env:
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_URL: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_URL }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN" ]; then
            echo "::warning::No SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: Sentry gets no debug files for this build, so its crashes show addresses only"
            exit 0
          fi
          case "$RUNNER_OS" in
            Windows) paths=(build/OrcaSlicer build/src/Release) ;;
            macOS) paths=("build/${{ inputs.arch }}/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents") ;;
            *) paths=(build/package/bin build/package/lib) ;;
          esac
          npx --yes @sentry/cli@3.8.2 debug-files upload --wait-for 600 "${paths[@]}"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.arch || 'x64' }}
          path: dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          # The release keeps the files; these only carry them to it.
          retention-days: 7

name: JusPrin build all

# Every platform of JusPrin from one commit, for jusprin_release.yml (a draft
# release) and jusprin_nightly.yml (the nightly-builds pre-release).
#
# Each platform is built by jusprin_release_build.yml; the macos job joins the
# two macOS architectures into the universal app and its disk image. The
# files are left as this run's artifacts named jusprin-*, for the caller to
# collect: the Windows x64 installer and portable zip, the macOS universal
# disk image, the Linux x64 AppImage, and the per-architecture Mac bundles,
# which only feed the universal app.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      version:
        required: true
        type: string
      # Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets JusPrin 1.x
      # used. Windows builds are unsigned.
      sign_macos:
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.name }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: Windows x64
            os: windows-latest
            arch: x64
          - name: macOS arm64
            os: macos-15
            arch: arm64
          - name: macOS x86_64
            os: macos-15
            arch: x86_64
          - name: Linux x64
            os: ubuntu-24.04
            arch: ''
    uses: ./.github/workflows/jusprin_release_build.yml
    with:
      os: ${{ matrix.os }}
      arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
      version: ${{ inputs.version }}
    secrets: inherit

  macos:
    name: macOS universal
    needs: build
    runs-on: macos-15
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      SIGN: ${{ inputs.sign_macos && '1' || '0' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      - name: Get both architectures
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-macOS-*
          path: mac_bundles
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Join them into the universal app
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/arm64 build/x86_64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_arm64.tar.gz -C build/arm64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_x86_64.tar.gz -C build/x86_64
          ./build_release_macos.sh -u -x -j 1 -a universal -t 10.15

      # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml loads the certificate, with the secret
      # names JusPrin 1.x used.
      - name: Load the signing certificate
        if: env.SIGN == '1'
        env:
          BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
          P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.P12_PASSWORD }}
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          certificate="$RUNNER_TEMP/build_certificate.p12"
          keychain="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          echo -n "$BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64" | base64 --decode --output "$certificate"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$keychain"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security default-keychain -s "$keychain"
          security import "$certificate" -P "$P12_PASSWORD" -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k "$keychain"
          security list-keychain -d user -s "$keychain"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$P12_PASSWORD" "$keychain"

      - name: Make the disk image
        env:
          JUSPRIN_SIGN: ${{ env.SIGN }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT }}
          TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.TEAM_ID }}
          APP_PWD: ${{ secrets.APP_PWD }}
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/macos_package.sh \
            build/universal/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app "$VERSION" dist

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-macOS-universal
          path: dist/*.dmg
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

1	name: JusPrin release
2	
3	# Builds JusPrin from one commit and uploads the files to a DRAFT GitHub
4	# release. It never publishes anything.
5	#
6	# - The version is the one in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp, and
7	#   the draft is tagged jusprin/v<version>, as JusPrin 1.4.0 was (the repo
8	#   still holds OrcaSlicer's own v2.x tags). GitHub creates that tag only when
9	#   the draft is published, by hand, on the Releases page. JusPrin's update
10	#   check reads the public release list, which never includes drafts, so
11	#   users see nothing until then.
12	# - It stops if that version is already released, is not above every
13	#   released JusPrin version, or its tag already exists
14	#   (Packaging/release.mjs), and if
15	#   Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md, the notes the draft starts with and
16	#   that the app shows under "What's new", is missing.
17	# - It also stops if the guide was not checked for this version
18	#   (docs/guide/checked-version.txt, written by scripts/check_guide.py
19	#   --ask-ai; see docs/guide/README.md), unless "Release without the guide
20	#   check" is ticked. Then the draft's title says the guide was not checked.
21	# - Running it again for the same version replaces the draft's files.
22	# - Files: Windows x64 installer and portable zip, macOS universal disk image,
23	#   Linux x64 AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
24	# - Only the release publisher can run it: the repo variable
25	#   JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER, or kennethjiang when it is unset.
26	# - Signing: macOS when "sign_macos" is ticked, with the Apple secrets JusPrin
27	#   1.x used. The box starts ticked: Homebrew's cask rules reject a Mac app
28	#   that is not signed and notarised. A release started by pushing a branch
29	#   is never signed. Windows builds are unsigned. An unsigned draft says so
30	#   in its title.
31	#
32	# Start it from Actions > JusPrin release > Run workflow (the file must also
33	# be on the default branch for that button), or by pushing a branch named
34	# jusprin-release/<anything>.
35	
36	on:
37	  workflow_dispatch:
38	    inputs:
39	      sign_macos:
40	        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
41	        type: boolean
42	        default: true
43	      skip_guide_check:
44	        description: 'Release without the guide check'
45	        type: boolean
46	        default: false
47	  push:
48	    branches:
49	      - 'jusprin-release/**'
50	
51	permissions:
52	  contents: write   # create the draft and upload its files
53	  actions: read
54	
55	concurrency:
56	  group: jusprin-release
57	  cancel-in-progress: false
58	
59	jobs:
60	  prepare:
61	    name: Check the version
62	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
63	    outputs:
64	      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
65	      tag: ${{ steps.check.outputs.tag }}
66	      prerelease: ${{ steps.check.outputs.prerelease }}
67	      draft_id: ${{ steps.check.outputs.draft_id }}
68	      guide_checked: ${{ steps.guide.outputs.checked }}
69	    steps:
70	      - name: Only the release publisher
71	        env:
72	          PUBLISHER: ${{ vars.JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER || 'kennethjiang' }}
73	        run: |
74	          if [ "$GITHUB_ACTOR" != "$PUBLISHER" ]; then
75	            echo "::error::Only @$PUBLISHER may make a JusPrin release (this run is @$GITHUB_ACTOR's)."
76	            exit 1
77	          fi
78	
79	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
80	        with:
81	          sparse-checkout: |
82	            src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin
83	            docs/guide
84	
85	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
86	        with:
87	          node-version: '24'
88	
89	      - name: Test the release checks
90	        run: node --test src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.test.mjs
91	
92	      - name: Check the version against the releases
93	        id: check
94	        env:
95	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
96	        run: |
97	          gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=100" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json"
98	          gh api --paginate "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/matching-refs/tags/" --jq '.[].ref' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt"
99	          node src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.mjs check src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp \
100	            "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json" "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
101	
102	      - name: Require the release notes
103	        run: |
104	          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}.md"
105	          if [ ! -s "$notes" ]; then
106	            echo "::error::Write $notes first. The draft starts with it and the app shows it under What's new."
107	            exit 1
108	          fi
109	          if grep -q '^PLACEHOLDER' "$notes"; then
110	            echo "::warning::$notes is still the placeholder. Replace it before publishing the draft."
111	          fi
112	
113	      - name: Require the guide check
114	        id: guide
115	        env:
116	          SKIP: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.skip_guide_check || false }}
117	        run: |
118	          problem=$(node src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.mjs guide src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp \
119	            docs/guide/checked-version.txt)
120	          if [ -z "$problem" ]; then
121	            echo "checked=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
122	          elif [ "$SKIP" = "true" ]; then
123	            echo "::warning::\"Release without the guide check\" is ticked, so the release goes on. $problem"
124	            echo "checked=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
125	          else
126	            echo "::error::$problem Or tick \"Release without the guide check\" on the Run workflow form."
127	            exit 1
128	          fi
129	
130	  build:
131	    name: Build
132	    needs: prepare
133	    uses: ./.github/workflows/jusprin_build_all.yml
134	    with:
135	      version: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
136	      sign_macos: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos || false }}
137	    secrets: inherit
138	
139	  draft:
140	    name: Upload to the draft release
141	    needs: [prepare, build]
142	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
143	    # Optional approval gate: give the "release" environment a required
144	    # reviewer in the repo settings.
145	    environment: release
146	    env:
147	      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
148	      VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
149	      TAG: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
150	      DRAFT_ID: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.draft_id }}
151	      PRERELEASE: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.prerelease }}
152	      SIGNED_MACOS: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos || false }}
153	      GUIDE_CHECKED: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.guide_checked }}
154	    steps:
155	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
156	        with:
157	          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging
158	
159	      - name: Collect the files
160	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
161	        with:
162	          pattern: jusprin-*
163	          path: collected
164	          merge-multiple: true
165	
166	      - name: Checksums
167	        run: |
168	          mkdir dist
169	          # The per-architecture Mac bundles only feed the universal app.
170	          find collected -maxdepth 1 -type f ! -name 'JusPrin_Mac_bundle_*' -exec cp {} dist/ \;
171	          (cd dist && sha256sum -- * > SHA256SUMS.txt)
172	          cat dist/SHA256SUMS.txt
173	
174	      - name: Create or update the draft
175	        run: |
176	          title="JusPrin $VERSION"
177	          if [ "$SIGNED_MACOS" != "true" ]; then
178	            title="$title (UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish)"
179	          fi
180	          if [ "$GUIDE_CHECKED" != "true" ]; then
181	            title="$title (guide not checked)"
182	          fi
183	          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/$VERSION.md"
184	          prerelease=$([ "$PRERELEASE" = "true" ] && echo --prerelease || echo --prerelease=false)
185	          if [ -z "$DRAFT_ID" ]; then
186	            gh release create "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft $prerelease \
187	              --target "$GITHUB_SHA" --title "$title" --notes-file "$notes"
188	          else
189	            # Never touch a published release: release.mjs only reports drafts.
190	            is_draft=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" --jq .draft)
191	            if [ "$is_draft" != "true" ]; then
192	              echo "::error::Release $DRAFT_ID is no longer a draft."
193	              exit 1
194	            fi
195	            gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" \
196	              -f target_commitish="$GITHUB_SHA" -f name="$title" -F prerelease="$PRERELEASE" \
197	              -f body="$(cat "$notes")" > /dev/null
198	            gh release upload "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
199	          fi
200	          gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=20" \
201	            --jq ".[] | select(.tag_name == \"$TAG\") | {name, draft, prerelease, target_commitish, html_url, assets: [.assets[].name]}"
202

1	name: JusPrin release build
2	
3	# One platform of a JusPrin release, called by jusprin_release.yml.
4	#
5	# The build is OrcaSlicer's: its dependency workflow (build_deps.yml), cached
6	# under the key OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml uses, and its build
7	# scripts. Only the packaging is JusPrin's (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging).
8	# OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml can't be reused as it is: its Linux step looks
9	# for OrcaSlicer_Linux_V<version>.AppImage, which a JusPrin build never
10	# writes, and its packaging steps name everything OrcaSlicer.
11	
12	on:
13	  workflow_call:
14	    inputs:
15	      os:
16	        required: true
17	        type: string
18	      # x64 (Windows), arm64 or x86_64 (macOS); empty for Linux amd64, as in
19	      # OrcaSlicer's build_all.yml.
20	      arch:
21	        required: false
22	        type: string
23	        default: ''
24	      version:
25	        required: true
26	        type: string
27	
28	jobs:
29	  cache:
30	    name: Find the deps cache
31	    # GitHub often has no hosted macOS runner free, and cancels a job that gets
32	    # none within 15 minutes, so the macOS lookup runs on Linux, as in
33	    # OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml.
34	    runs-on: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && 'ubuntu-24.04' || inputs.os }}
35	    outputs:
36	      key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
37	      path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
38	      hit: ${{ steps.lookup.outputs.cache-hit }}
39	    steps:
40	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
41	        with:
42	          lfs: 'false'
43	      - name: Compute the key
44	        id: key
45	        shell: bash
46	        env:
47	          # As in OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml. The macOS and Linux trees are
48	          # OrcaSlicer's and share its cache; OrcaSlicer builds Windows with clang-cl,
49	          # so JusPrin's cl tree is cached on its own.
50	          cache_os: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && format('{0}-{1}', inputs.os, inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && format('windows-{0}-msvc', inputs.arch) || format('linux-clang{0}', inputs.arch && format('-{0}', inputs.arch) || '')) }}
51	          OS: ${{ inputs.os }}
52	          dep_folder: ${{ startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos-') && format('/{0}', inputs.arch) || (runner.os == 'Windows' && inputs.arch == 'arm64') && '-arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep' || '/OrcaSlicer_dep' }}
53	        run: |
54	          echo "key=${cache_os}-cache-orcaslicer_deps-build-${{ hashFiles('deps/**') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
55	          # Relative to the workspace, as build_deps.yml takes it.
56	          echo "path=deps/build${dep_folder}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
57	          # The workspace of a hosted macOS job, where build_deps.yml saved the tree.
58	          if [[ "$OS" == macos-* ]]; then
59	            echo "macos_workspace=/Users/runner/work/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY#*/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
60	          fi
61	      # actions/cache matches the path too, so a Linux lookup for macOS names the
62	      # macOS workspace.
63	      - name: Look the cache up
64	        id: lookup
65	        uses: actions/cache@v5
66	        with:
67	          path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.macos_workspace || github.workspace }}/${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
68	          key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
69	          lookup-only: true
70	
71	  deps:
72	    name: Build deps
73	    needs: cache
74	    if: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.hit != 'true' }}

5	#
6	# Each platform is built by jusprin_release_build.yml; the macos job joins the
7	# two macOS architectures into the universal app and its disk image. The
8	# files are left as this run's artifacts named jusprin-*, for the caller to
9	# collect: the Windows x64 installer and portable zip, the macOS universal

14	  workflow_call:
15	    inputs:
16	      version:
17	        required: true
18	        type: string

46	    with:

49	      version: ${{ inputs.version }}

51	
52	  macos:
53	    name: macOS universal
54	    needs: build
55	    runs-on: macos-15
56	    env:
57	      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}

59	    steps:
60	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
61	        with:
62	          lfs: 'false'
63	
64	      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest

66	          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
67	          useLocalCache: true
68	          useCloudCache: true
69	
70	      - name: Get both architectures

72	        with:

76

80	          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_arm64.tar.gz -C build/arm64
81	          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_x86_64.tar.gz -C build/x86_64
82	          ./build_release_macos.sh -u -x -j 1 -a universal -t 10.15
83

# Gives Sentry what it needs to name the functions in a JusPrin crash or error
# report: the debug files of one platform's build (jusprin_release_build.yml),

name: JusPrin nightly

# Builds jusprin-dev, the development branch, once a day and puts the files
# on the "nightly-builds" pre-release, replacing the day before's, as
# JusPrin 1's "Build all" did.
#
# - GitHub runs scheduled workflows only on the default branch, main. The
#   scheduled run therefore only starts this workflow again on jusprin-dev,
#   so every step, OrcaSlicer's dependency build included, checks out
#   jusprin-dev.
# - The build is the release's (jusprin_build_all.yml), so a nightly is what a
#   release from the same commit would be. Its version is the one in
#   src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp.
# - The files keep JusPrin 1's nightly names, so download links stay the
#   same: JusPrin_Windows_Installer_nightly.exe,
#   JusPrin_Windows_nightly_portable.zip, JusPrin_Mac_universal_nightly.dmg,
#   JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_nightly.AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - The nightly-builds tag moves to the commit built, and the release notes
#   name it. The scheduled build is skipped when jusprin-dev has not changed
#   since the last nightly.
# - The macOS app is signed and notarised; Windows builds are unsigned.
# - The app's update check never offers a nightly: it reads only tags named
#   vX.Y.Z and jusprin/vX.Y.Z (ReleaseFeed.cpp).
# - GitHub's hosted Apple-silicon macOS runners are often all taken in US
#   daytime, and GitHub cancels a job that gets none within 15 minutes. The
#   scheduled run lands in those hours, because this repo's schedules start
#   hours late. A run whose only failures are such jobs starts the nightly
#   again, up to 8 runs a day for one commit.
#
# Run it by hand from Actions > JusPrin nightly > Run workflow, with the
# branch set to jusprin-dev.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '35 7 * * *' # near midnight US Pacific time, as JusPrin 1's nightly
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign_macos:
        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
        type: boolean

content.content:
1	---
2	name: jusprin-release
3	description: Use when asked to make, prepare or start a new JusPrin release (a new version on GitHub), from choosing the commit range to the after-publish steps. Covers the version, release notes, server readiness, translations, the error-handling audit, tests, the guide check, moving main, the release workflow, testing the draft and what follows publishing. Not for JusPrin 1 (jusprin-v1) or OrcaSlicer's own releases.
4	---
5	
6	# Making a JusPrin release
7	
8	The release workflow, `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`, builds the
9	release files from one commit and uploads them to a draft release on GitHub.
10	It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes and a guide check
11	(see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not run the test suites, check the
12	server, check the translations or audit error handling. This skill covers
13	those too, in the order they have to happen.
14	
15	## Kenneth decides these
16	
17	Ask Kenneth, in plain words, and wait for his yes before each of these. A yes
18	covers that one action, not the next one.
19	
20	- The version number, when he has not named it.
21	- The release notes' wording. Show him the file.
22	- Deploying the server.
23	- Spending API money on live AI checks. Say the cost.
24	- Pushing to `jusprin-dev`, and moving `main` forward.
25	- Starting the release workflow.
26	- Downloading the draft's files to this computer.
27	- Posting anything on GitHub, such as replies to issues.
28	
29	**Never publish the draft.** Kenneth publishes it by hand on the Releases page.
30	Never force-push `main`.
31	
32	## 1. Set up
33	
34	1. Check that the main checkout (the folder that holds `jusprin-dev`, not a
35	   worktree) has nothing that would be left out of the release:
36	
37	   ```bash
38	   git -C <main checkout> fetch origin
39	   git -C <main checkout> status --porcelain -uno
40	   git -C <main checkout> log --oneline origin/jusprin-dev..jusprin-dev
41	   ```
42	
43	   Both must print nothing. A changed file or a commit that is not on GitHub
44	   is work someone may expect in the release. Stop, list each one for
45	   Kenneth, and wait until he has pushed it or said to leave it out. Do not
46	   push, commit or discard it yourself. Untracked files do not block: they
47	   are working docs Kenneth keeps there on purpose.
48	2. Find the last release: `git tag --list 'jusprin/v*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1`.
49	   The range is that tag to `origin/jusprin-dev` (after `git fetch origin`).
50	3. Make your own worktree from `origin/jusprin-dev`, under
51	   `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`, on a branch named `claude/release-<version>`.
52	   Never name it `jusprin-release/...`: pushing a branch with that name starts
53	   an unsigned release build.
54	4. Read every commit in the range: `git log --format='%h %s%n%b' <range>`.
55	   Note what a person would notice, and the GitHub issues each change fixes.
56	
57	## 2. Version and release notes
58	
59	1. Set `kVersion` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`. It must be
60	   above every released JusPrin version.
61	2. Write `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`. The app
62	   shows this file under "What's new", and the draft starts with it. Follow the
63	   shape of the previous release's file. Write for a person who prints, not for
64	   a developer. Check every on-screen label you quote against the source
65	   (`git grep`), and leave out anything you have not checked.
66	3. A change that sends anything new from the person's computer, such as a new
67	   message to our server, goes in the notes and says what it holds.
68	
69	## 3. Server readiness
70	
71	The app calls JusPrin's server at `https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. Every address
72	the release calls must already be deployed there.
73	
74	```bash

---
name: jusprin-release
description: Use when asked to make, prepare or start a new JusPrin release (a new version on GitHub), from choosing the commit range to the after-publish steps. Covers the version, release notes, server readiness, translations, the error-handling audit, tests, the guide check, moving main, the release workflow, testing the draft and what follows publishing. Not for JusPrin 1 (jusprin-v1) or OrcaSlicer's own releases.
---

# Making a JusPrin release

The release workflow, `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`, builds the
release files from one commit and uploads them to a draft release on GitHub.
It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes and a guide check
(see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not run the test suites, check the
server, check the translations or audit error handling. This skill covers
those too, in the order they have to happen.

## Kenneth decides these

Ask Kenneth, in plain words, and wait for his yes before each of these. A yes
covers that one action, not the next one.

- The version number, when he has not named it.
- The release notes' wording. Show him the file.
- Deploying the server.
- Spending API money on live AI checks. Say the cost.
- Pushing to `jusprin-dev`, and moving `main` forward.
- Starting the release workflow.
- Downloading the draft's files to this computer.
- Posting anything on GitHub, such as replies to issues.

**Never publish the draft.** Kenneth publishes it by hand on the Releases page.
Never force-push `main`.

## 1. Set up

1. Check that the main checkout (the folder that holds `jusprin-dev`, not a
   worktree) has nothing that would be left out of the release:

   ```bash
   git -C <main checkout> fetch origin
   git -C <main checkout> status --porcelain -uno
   git -C <main checkout> log --oneline origin/jusprin-dev..jusprin-dev
   ```

   Both must print nothing. A changed file or a commit that is not on GitHub
   is work someone may expect in the release. Stop, list each one for
   Kenneth, and wait until he has pushed it or said to leave it out. Do not
   push, commit or discard it yourself. Untracked files do not block: they
   are working docs Kenneth keeps there on purpose.
2. Find the last release: `git tag --list 'jusprin/v*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1`.
   The range is that tag to `origin/jusprin-dev` (after `git fetch origin`).
3. Make your own worktree from `origin/jusprin-dev`, under
   `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`, on a branch named `claude/release-<version>`.
   Never name it `jusprin-release/...`: pushing a branch with that name starts
   an unsigned release build.
4. Read every commit in the range: `git log --format='%h %s%n%b' <range>`.
   Note what a person would notice, and the GitHub issues each change fixes.

## 2. Version and release notes

1. Set `kVersion` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`. It must be
   above every released JusPrin version.
2. Write `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`. The app
   shows this file under "What's new", and the draft starts with it. Follow the
   shape of the previous release's file. Write for a person who prints, not for
   a developer. Check every on-screen label you quote against the source
   (`git grep`), and leave out anything you have not checked.
3. A change that sends anything new from the person's computer, such as a new
   message to our server, goes in the notes and says what it holds.

## 3. Server readiness

The app calls JusPrin's server at `https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. Every address
the release calls must already be deployed there.

```bash
git grep -h -o '"/ent/jusprin/v2/[a-z_/]*' -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin ':!*test*' | tr -d '"' | sort -u
```

GET each one: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://jusprinv2.obico.io<path>`.
Any answer but 404 (200, 401, 403, 405) means the address is there. A 404
means it is not deployed. Find the server change in the tsd-enterprise
repository (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py` on `master`), tell Kenneth what is
missing, and wait until it is deployed. Also tell him about any other server
behavior a change in the range relies on, such as a new error code.

## 4. Translations

1. Run `python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py`. It
   needs GNU gettext and `npm ci` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`. If it
   changes any catalog, those changes go into the release commit.
2. Translate every new entry in every language, following "Localization &
   translations" in `AGENTS.md` and the `orca-translations` skill.
3. `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts` in `AgentUI` must pass: it fails
   while an entry is untranslated or a translation lost a placeholder.
4. Count the entries marked `# Needs human review` in
   `Localization/native/*.po` and `Localization/pages/*.po`. Tell Kenneth the
   count, so he can decide whether someone should read a language.

These steps cannot find a sentence nobody marked for translation. While
reading the range, look for text a person reads that is not marked.

## 5. Error-handling audit

Run the `error-handling` skill on the range. When the release relies on
server changes, audit the tsd-enterprise range too. Report the findings to
Kenneth. A fix lands on `jusprin-dev` as its own commit, and the steps above
are then repeated for the new range.

## 6. Tests

Build in your worktree, in Release, following "Building on a shared machine"
in `AGENTS.md`: check the load first, use `-j4`, choose every target before
you start. Configure with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON`.

- macOS: build `agent_bridge_tests`, `jusprin_tests`, `shell_integration_harness`,
  `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs`, then run both test programs and
  `npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI`.
- Windows and Linux: the release workflow compiles them but runs no tests.
  Run `agent_bridge_tests` and `jusprin_tests` on each. Kenneth keeps test
  machines for both; ask him for access if you do not have it, and say in
  your report if they were not run.
- When the range changes text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool
  descriptions, tool results, how history is sent), run the live prompt suite
  (`tests/project_prompt/README.md`, and `tests/printer_prompt` when printer
  chats changed). Its `claude-cli` backend costs no API money. Any run that
  spends API money needs Kenneth's yes first.

Report each failure with its output. A failure in the range is a bug to fix
on `jusprin-dev` before the release, not a reason to skip the step.

## 7. Guide check

Follow "Before a release" in `docs/guide/README.md`, on the build from step 6
with the new version already in `Version.hpp`.

1. Tell Kenneth first: the command drives the app on this computer's screen
   for about a minute a page, so nobody should use the computer meanwhile.
2. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` and fix what it reports until it
   passes. It then writes the version to `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`.
3. Look through `git log <range> -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` for new screens or
   menu items no page mentions, and add them to the guide.

## 8. Commit and land

1. Commit the version, the notes, the catalogs and the guide files on your
   branch. Make sure no temporary working docs or screenshots are in it.
2. With Kenneth's yes, land it on `jusprin-dev` without a merge commit: rebase
   onto `origin/jusprin-dev`, then `git push origin HEAD:jusprin-dev`. Then
   bring the main checkout along: `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`.
3. With Kenneth's yes, move `main` to the same commit:
   `git push origin origin/jusprin-dev:main`. This only succeeds as a fast
   forward. If it is refused, stop and tell Kenneth. Never force it.

## 9. Start the release workflow

Only Kenneth's GitHub account may run it; check with `gh api user -q .login`.
With his yes:

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
```

Keep Mac signing on: Homebrew refuses a Mac app that is not signed and
notarised. Wait for the run in the background (`gh run watch <id>`). A failed
run is a failure to report with its log, not a reason to tick a skip box.

## 10. Test the draft

The draft holds the Windows installer and portable zip, the Mac disk image,
the Linux AppImage and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. These files are what people will get,
so test them, not a local build. Ask Kenneth before downloading them.

On each platform: install over the previous release and start the app. Check
that Preferences shows the new version, sign in, have one chat, slice, and
check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered (for example a
locale bug on Windows, where it always shows). Send one error report if the
release changed reporting.

Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform and what was not. He publishes.

## 11. After publishing

- Start the previous release on one computer and check that Preferences ›
  Updates offers the new version. The update check reads only published
  releases, so this is the first moment it can be checked.
- Reply to and close the GitHub issues the release fixes, with Kenneth's yes.
- Update JusPrin's Homebrew cask to the new version, if the cask is in
  Homebrew.
- The next day, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise
  repository for new failures from the new version.
- Remove your worktree and branch.

content.content:
## Releasing

`.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` builds a release into a draft on GitHub; its top comment says how to start it. It refuses the commit until it has all of these:

- The version, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`, above every released JusPrin version.
- The release notes, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`.
- The Sentry secrets: `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, the project the app sends error reports and crashes to, and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT`, which upload each build's debug files. A platform's build fails unless Sentry then holds function names for the app's own code (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh`); the nightly build checks the same.
- The guide, `docs/guide/`, checked for that version. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` on a built copy of the commit, fix every page it reports, and commit the pages with their pictures, skills and `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`, as `docs/guide/README.md` describes under "Before a release". That file names the version the check last passed for, not the commit. Ticking "Release without the guide check" on the workflow's Run workflow form skips this, and the draft's title then says so. A release started by pushing a `jusprin-release/` branch has no form, so it always needs the file.
